summary: Cached operand delivery limits performance, rather than DRAM bandwidth or compute throughput.
reasoning: Memory SOL is 69.59% versus 38.1% compute SOL. L2 throughput reaches 74.27% with a 95.71% hit rate, while DRAM throughput is only 15.59%. Long-scoreboard stalls of 62.67% indicate substantial waits for memory dependencies.

root_causes.cause: The small 32×64 output tiles provide limited operand reuse, increasing traffic through the heavily used L2 cache.

evidence.interpretation: L2 is the most heavily utilized reported memory level.
Most accesses hit L2; low DRAM utilization does not rule out a cached-memory bottleneck.

fixes.fix: Autotune larger output tiles, including 64×64 and 64×128, together with num_warps.
fixes.rationale: Larger tiles reuse each loaded operand across more output elements, reducing cache traffic per operation; tuning is needed to avoid excessive register and shared-memory pressure.

root_causes.cause: Partial global-load sector utilization wastes transfer capacity and contributes to memory-dependency stalls.

evidence.interpretation: Global loads use only half of the transferred sector bytes on average.
Warps frequently wait for outstanding memory dependencies.

fixes.fix: Specialize operand loading for the actual input strides so adjacent lanes access adjacent FP16/BF16 elements along the contiguous dimension.
fixes.rationale: Better coalescing can increase useful bytes per sector and reduce memory transactions and associated waits.
